neighbours.label: ' other' (or ' in') right after 'work(s) (closely) with/in' in a job description, awaiting who or what one works with
fire: Paralegals work closely with other lawyers to prepare each case.
Dental hygienists work alongside other clinicians in the practice.
Site managers work closely with other contractors to keep the project on time.
Librarians work together with other teachers to plan the reading lessons.
Payroll clerks work closely with other departments to fix pay errors.
Pharmacists work with other health professionals to review each prescription.
Stage managers work closely with other crew members during rehearsals.
Social workers work with other agencies to find housing for families.
quiet: Paralegals often read the other side's papers before each case.
Dental hygienists see one patient after the other all morning.
Site managers checked the plans against other drawings from last year.
Librarians moved the atlases to the other end of the reading room.
Payroll clerks found two other errors in the March figures.
Pharmacists keep some other medicines in a locked cabinet.
Stage managers arrived every other day during rehearsals.
Social workers visited three other families on the same street.

notes: Card: ' in', ' of', ' various', ' other', ' another', ' latest' before a noun; both poles look alike. Probes: 'Nurses work closely with other staff' 0.74, 'works in this trade' 0.23, 'count of various cells' 0.24, 'the latest on' 0.35, but 'compared it with other brands' 0.03 and 'another kind of' 0.00. The work-with frame is the best guess; near misses keep ' other' outside it.
